Cimini at Wednesday practice: no sign of Breece Hall, not even in the rehab area.

items.opportunity: Thursday and Friday practice participation and the Friday injury designation decide Hall's status; Allen's role grows only if Hall sits.

items.text: #Browns Todd Monken is optimistic that both Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson will face the #Titans on Sunday.
items.priorStatus: Sampson IR stash, return timing TBD; Judkins nearing return (radio, Tue)
items.why: Head coach Todd Monken said Wednesday he is optimistic both Browns backs play Sunday vs. Tennessee. This upgrades Tuesday's radio-only expectation, which was held below floor. Browns listed Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Dylan Sampson (knee) as limited participants Wednesday (UnderdogNFL; RotoWire via Akron Beacon Journal). Thu 12:17 PM ET: Browns OC Travis Switzer said it's "huge" to have Judkins (ankle) and Sampson (knee) both back this week vs. the Titans to provide a one-two punch (Mary Kay Cabot).
items.implication: Both could be back for Week 7, which would split the Browns backfield between them. Neither is officially cleared yet; practice reports will show it.
items.opportunity: Watch Wednesday-Friday practice participation and any IR activation move for Sampson before Sunday.

items.text: Source: The Giants plan to start J.J. McCarthy on Sunday vs. Houston.
items.priorStatus: Winston vs. McCarthy Week 7 decision pending
items.why: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports, citing a source, that the Giants plan to start McCarthy over Winston Sunday vs. Houston. No official team announcement yet. Harbaugh confirmed Wednesday: "We will be starting J.J. (McCarthy) in the game" vs. Texans; Jameis Winston is the backup (Jordan Raanan; also Schefter, Garafolo, Rapoport). Harbaugh added that starting McCarthy is the plan going forward (PFT). McCarthy stayed after Wednesday practice for extra work with his starting receivers, including Malik Nabers (Jordan Raanan). Raanan: McCarthy is the Giants starting quarterback for the foreseeable future; Harbaugh met with the QBs one-on-one Tuesday.
items.implication: Backup QB promoted to the starting job, which shifts the Giants passing game outlook to McCarthy for Week 7.
items.opportunity: QB role change on a team-wide basis; confirm with the Giants' official announcement or head coach comments.

items.text: Saints GM Mickey Loomis said WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) is improving and 'getting closer' but will not practice this week.
items.priorStatus: IR (return window possible as soon as Oct 21)
items.why: GM statement Wednesday, confirmed by the official Saints account and Schefter. Tyson has not played a snap this season; no practice window opens this week.
items.implication: Tyson cannot be activated for Week 7, so the Saints WR rotation Vele has been working in stays without him this week. Dwain McFarland noted Tyson's return would cut into Vele's targets, so that risk is pushed back at least a week.
items.opportunity: Vele's current WR role is unchanged for Week 7; Tyson's earliest return now looks like Week 8 or later.

items.text: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said WR Christian Kirk (calf, IR) is a possibility to play in Week 7 at ATL; he does not think WR Demarcus Robinson will be ready to come off IR.
items.why: Head coach comment in MNF postgame presser (Mon night). No official activation or practice window yet. Update Wed 10-21: Kirk (calf) was listed as a full participant on the 49ers' Wednesday report, his first full participation this season (Nick Wagoner, ESPN; Harrison Rich). The session was a walkthrough after the Monday game, so participation was estimated. He remains on IR until activated.
items.implication: Kirk could rejoin a thin SF WR room (Evans Achilles tendinitis, Deebo Samuel hamstring) for Week 7 at ATL; first confirmation would be a practice-window opening and Wed/Thu participation.
items.opportunity: If activated, immediate target opportunity in an SF passing game missing multiple WRs.

items.text: Shanahan on Mike Evans: same Achilles issue that bothered him all week, acted up during MNF; called it Achilles tendinitis, not a long-term thing, no further testing believed needed. Week 7 availability at ATL unclear (PFT: hopeful he can play Sunday).
items.why: Head coach postgame comments; supersedes Monday-night aggravated-Achilles item with severity unknown. Evans (Achilles, ribs) did not practice Wednesday, as expected (Matt Barrows; also Nick Wagoner).
items.implication: Serious injury appears avoided, but Evans did not practice all last week and Week 7 status is uncertain; watch Wed practice participation.
items.opportunity: If Evans is limited or out, SF targets shift toward McCaffrey/Kittle and any returning WR (Christian Kirk).

items.text: Commanders HC Dan Quinn said WR Terry McLaurin tore his left patellar tendon (MRI Tuesday) and will miss the rest of the season. Team account confirmed the season-ending injury.
items.why: Head coach confirmation after the MRI, posted by the Commanders and the WAS beat; resolves the Monday-night UNCONFIRMED_HIGH_PRIORITY item (same event, superseded).
items.implication: Washington loses its WR1 for the season. WAS is on a Week 7 bye, so the WR target share is redistributed from Week 8; no coach has named who moves into the lead WR role yet. Watch for an IR move, a WR addition, and post-bye depth chart.
items.opportunity: Season-long vacated WR1 target share in Washington from Week 8.

items.text: 49ers WR routes on 34 Brock Purdy dropbacks in MNF Week 6 vs WAS: Jordan Watkins 31, Brandin Cooks 16, Mike Evans 16 (left early, heel), Jacob Cowing 11, Malik Turner 1. Deebo Samuel, Christian Kirk, Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling were all out injured.
items.why: Player-specific route participation from MNF (91% of dropbacks) with five SF WRs injured; usage data, not a depth-chart announcement. Wednesday: Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) did not practice (Nick Wagoner, Shanahan's practice plan).
items.implication: Watkins was SF's only near-every-down WR on MNF. Week 7 role depends on Evans (Achilles/heel) and Kirk (calf, IR, possible return) status; a Kirk activation would compete for the same routes.
items.opportunity: Near-full-time route share in a depleted SF WR room heading into Week 7 at ATL.

items.text: The Giants are releasing RB Najee Harris. Harris was named the Week 6 starter vs. New Orleans but had 4 carries for 2 yards; he has 31 carries for 99 yards (3.2 per carry) this season. It follows his public frustration with John Harbaugh's four-back rotation.
items.why: Starter in a four-back rotation removed from the roster; the Giants backfield goes from four backs to three heading into Week 7.
items.implication: Harris's carries move to the remaining Giants backs. No coach has named a lead back yet; watch Wednesday practice and Harbaugh comments for who gets the bigger share.
items.opportunity: Fewer backs splitting Giants carries; possible role growth for the remaining NYG RBs.
supportingSources: Dan Duggan (The Athletic, snap-count note on the four-back rotation)

items.text: Texans are waiving LB Jamal Hill from the 53-man roster to open a roster spot for the pending activation of WR Tank Dell, per a league source.
items.why: HOU beat roster-move report: the Texans are clearing a 53-man spot specifically for Dell's activation, the step before he is officially added back. DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Dell will play in Week 7. Aaron Wilson: Tank Dell back on the practice field Wednesday. DeMeco Ryans on Tank Dell's return: excited for Sunday to see him run out of the tunnel (Aaron Wilson).
items.implication: Dell is on track to rejoin the Houston WR rotation for Week 7 after his long injury absence; the official activation would confirm it. His snap and route share on return is not yet known.
items.opportunity: A returning WR who could move back into a regular role in the Houston passing game from Week 7.

items.text: Eagles waived RB Jaydon Blue and placed RB Carson Steele on waived/injured, and signed RB Elijah Mitchell to the practice squad. That leaves Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce as the only running backs on the 53-man roster.
items.why: PHI beat and national reports of official roster moves. Pierce was elevated to carry the workload in Week 6 with Barkley out; with Blue and Steele gone he is now the only other running back on the active roster. Barkley's Week 7 status has not been announced.
items.implication: Pierce is the clear No. 2 back in Philadelphia, and the lead back if Barkley misses Week 7 against Dallas. Field Yates reads the thin room as a sign Barkley may be back for Week 7; that is analyst inference, not a team statement.
items.opportunity: Backup promoted to sole RB2, with lead-back carries if Barkley is out.

items.text: The Bucs are game planning as if Jalon Daniels will start Sunday at Carolina. Baker Mayfield (dislocated thumb) will practice Wednesday for the first time since the injury, and the team moved its weekly QB media availability to Thursday.
items.why: TB beat report, matching Greg Auman's account of Todd Bowles saying the team will plan initially on Daniels starting while it evaluates Mayfield. Mayfield returns to practice Wednesday; no final Week 7 decision yet. Bowles expects to decide on Mayfield Friday; Mayfield threw well Wednesday and the QBs split reps (Jenna Laine; also PFT). Buccaneers listed Baker Mayfield (right thumb) as a full participant Wednesday (Schefter; also UnderdogNFL). Bowles still expects to decide Friday.
items.implication: Daniels is the working Week 7 starter against Carolina unless Mayfield's thumb progresses this week. Thursday's QB availability is the next checkpoint.
items.opportunity: Backup QB in line to start Week 7; role depends on Mayfield's Wednesday/Thursday practice.
